commit_reviews.summary: A clean plugin-architecture refactor that extracts markdown/template rendering and dev-server live-reload out of generator.ts while preserving exports for compatibility.

compounding_issues: Session 1 built a monolith (generator.ts ~110 lines with inline HTML templating) with no seam for templating, so Session 2 had to bolt the template engine onto it rather than through a defined interface, forcing the big Session 4 refactor

Session 2 hand-rolled a regex-based Handlebars/EJS subset ({{#each}}, {{#if}}, partials, EJS tags) instead of adding handlebars/ejs dependencies — lower feature fidelity and escaping edge-case risk, and the code had to be carried forward through two subsequent sessions

Session 3's dev server was written standalone (server.ts, 125 lines) with live-reload injection independent of the build pipeline, and Session 4 had to retrofit it into the plugin system (re-wrote server.ts + new dev-server-plugin.ts), a remediation not present in the original design

Session 4's plugin layer introduced a circular import (plugin.ts imports BuildOptions/Page from generator.ts; generator.ts imports Plugin from plugin.ts) plus a WeakMap metadata side-channel (pageMetadata/parsedPages in markdown-plugin.ts) that Session 5 had to thread cache state through
ssg.config.ts plugins are loaded via runtime require(), which works for CommonJS/ts-jest but couples the CLI to CJS resolution
key_decisions: Session 4's plugin architecture with lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) — the pivotal decision that made Session 5's incremental builds clean; Session 5 consumed changedOutputs/stats from the plugin context instead of adding parallel machinery
Session 2's choice to hand-roll a template engine with HTML escaping rather than pull in handlebars/ejs — kept deps lean (gray-matter, marked, chokidar, ws only) at the cost of feature fidelity

Session 5's hash-based cache design: .ssg-cache.json manifest keyed by source + template hashes, full-invalidate on template change, and cache reuse wired through plugin context rather than as a separate code path
Session 1's greenfield rewrite of a mismatched seed (Express Todo API) into a TypeScript SSG from scratch — the seed offered no foundation, so all architecture originated in Session 1
Tiered output via date-sorted pages + always-written index.html, giving the site stable, deterministic structure across feature additions
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily, with a structural step-change at Session 4. Session 1 produced a clean but monolithic greenfield SSG with 3 passing tests. Session 2 added templating (regex HBS/EJS) that worked but grew the monolith and duplicated rendering concerns, expanding tests to 5. Session 3 shipped a functional live-reload dev server but kept it coupled to the generator. Session 4 was the peak: a 224-line reduction of generator.ts into four plugin modules (markdown/template/dev-server/plugin) — high-risk refactor that preserved behavior and test parity. Session 5 then delivered the hardest feature, incremental builds with hash caching and template invalidation, cleanly on the plugin architecture and grew tests to 7 including a full cache-skip/invalidate/clean cycle. The refactor's payoff is visible in Session 5, which adds 106 lines to generator.ts without disturbing the plugin contracts. The main blemish is a small circular-import / global WeakMap smell in the plugin layer and the hand-rolled template engine's fidelity limits, but overall the arc is one of disciplined, improving engineering.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent five-session arc that follows greenfield → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting, culminating in a strong incremental-build session that was only possible because Session 4's plugin refactor created the right seams — the primary compounding cost was Session 1/2's monolith and hand-rolled template engine, which Session 4 had to dismantle.
